views.name: qualifying_attempts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  qualifyId,
  raceId,
  driverId,
  q1,
  CASE
    WHEN q1 IS NOT NULL AND q1 != '' THEN
      (
        -- convert q1 formatted as M:SS.mmm or MM:SS.mmm or SS.mmm to milliseconds
        (CAST(substr(q1, 1, instr(q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000)
        + (CAST(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1, instr(q1, '.') - instr(q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
        + CAST(substr(q1, instr(q1, '.') + 1) AS INTEGER)
      )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS q1_milliseconds,
  q2,
  q3,
  position,
  number,
  constructorId
FROM qualifying

params.description: Provides one-row-per-qualifying-attempt details (qualifyId) including raw lap time strings and a computed q1 time in milliseconds.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve qualifying attempt details for a specific qualifyId or raceId | List all qualifying attempts for a race or driver with q1 converted to milliseconds for sorting/comparison | Compose queries that need per-qualify-attempt attributes (position, driverId, constructorId, number) as a stable grain | Aggregate qualifying attempts (counts, averages of q1_milliseconds) by driver, constructor, or race when this view is used as the starting grain
params.output_schema: qualifyId: unique identifier for this qualifying attempt (base column: qualifying.qualifyId) — the row grain | raceId: identifier of the race this qualifying attempt belongs to (base column: qualifying.raceId) | driverId: identifier of the driver who made the attempt (base column: qualifying.driverId) | q1: raw qualifying lap time string for Q1 as stored (base column: qualifying.q1), formatted like M:SS.mmm or SS.mmm | q1_milliseconds: q1 converted to integer milliseconds (derived metric computed from qualifying.q1 using string parsing and arithmetic); NULL when q1 is NULL or empty | q2: raw qualifying lap time string for Q2 (base column: qualifying.q2) | q3: raw qualifying lap time string for Q3 (base column: qualifying.q3) | position: qualifying position for this attempt (base column: qualifying.position) | number: car number for this attempt (base column: qualifying.number) | constructorId: identifier of the constructor/team for this attempt (base column: qualifying.constructorId)
params.grounded_columns: qualifying.qualifyId | qualifying.raceId | qualifying.driverId | qualifying.q1 | qualifying.q2 | qualifying.q3 | qualifying.position | qualifying.number | qualifying.constructorId
params.metric: q1_milliseconds = CASE WHEN qualifying.q1 IS NOT NULL AND qualifying.q1 != '' THEN (CAST(substr(qualifying.q1, 1, instr(qualifying.q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000) + (CAST(substr(qualifying.q1, instr(qualifying.q1, ':') + 1, instr(qualifying.q1, '.') - instr(qualifying.q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 1000) + CAST(substr(qualifying.q1, instr(qualifying.q1, '.') + 1) AS INTEGER) ELSE NULL END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a race dimension/view on raceId — safe because this view is one-row-per-qualifyId; joining to a race (one row per raceId) will not duplicate qualifying measures | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a driver dimension/view on driverId — safe because driver is a one-row-per-driver dimension; it will not duplicate this view's rows or measures | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a constructor/team dimension/view on constructorId — safe for the same reason (one-row-per-constructor) | unsafe join warning: do NOT join this view directly to tables or views that are one-to-many from qualifyId (for example a hypothetical telemetry/lap_times table keyed by qualifyId with multiple rows) without first aggregating the many-side to qualifyId and re-aggregating metrics. Such joins would multiply rows and distort aggregates like counts or averages derived from q1_milliseconds | unsafe join warning: when joining to other event-level tables that have multiple rows per driver-per-race (for example practice sessions, incidents), ensure you aggregate those tables to the same grain (qualifyId or driverId+raceId) before joining to avoid duplicating this view's measures | aggregation guidance: to compute aggregates over drivers or constructors, GROUP BY driverId or constructorId using this view as the source (e.g., AVG(q1_milliseconds) by driverId) rather than joining to many-side tables which would require DISTINCT or additional aggregation to remain correct

params.output_schema: driverId: unique surrogate identifier for a driver — derives directly from drivers.driverId | driverRef: textual driver reference/code — derives directly from drivers.driverRef | forename: driver's given name — derives directly from drivers.forename | surname: driver's family name — derives directly from drivers.surname | number: racing number assigned to the driver — derives directly from drivers.number | dob: driver's date of birth — derives directly from drivers.dob | nationality: driver's nationality string — derives directly from drivers.nationality

params.metric: This view exposes no derived aggregations; all columns are base attributes. Example composed metric (to be defined in downstream queries): attempts_by_driver = COUNT(qualifying_attempts.attemptId) GROUP BY driverId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables or views that are 1:1 or many:1 to driverId (for example, other driver-master views) on drivers.driverId — safe because drivers.driverId is one-row-per-driver so the view's attributes will not be duplicated. | Safe to join to aggregated driver-level metrics (for example, qualifying_attempts aggregated to driverId) on driverId — the aggregations must be performed first so rows remain one-per-driver. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed by driverId (for example, raw qualifying_attempts without aggregation) without re-aggregating or de-duplicating first, because such joins will multiply driver rows and thereby duplicate any driver-level measures or counts. | When composing with event- or attempt-level facts, either aggregate the facts to driverId before joining this view, or use EXISTS/IN or windowed DISTINCT constructions to avoid inflating driver-level measures.

views.name: qualifying_with_driver_ref
views.body_sql:

  q.qualifyId,

params.output_schema: qualifyId: unique identifier of the qualifying attempt, derived from qualifying_attempts.qualifyId | raceId: identifier of the race this qualifying attempt belongs to, derived from qualifying_attempts.raceId | driverId: identifier of the driver who made the qualifying attempt, derived from qualifying_attempts.driverId | driverRef: short driver reference/code, derived from drivers_base.driverRef | forename: driver's forename (given name), derived from drivers_base.forename | surname: driver's surname (family name), derived from drivers_base.surname | q1: textual or numeric representation of the Q1 lap time as stored, derived from qualifying_attempts.q1 | q1_milliseconds: q1 lap time expressed in milliseconds (stored as-is in the base table), derived from qualifying_attempts.q1_milliseconds | q2: textual or numeric representation of the Q2 lap time as stored, derived from qualifying_attempts.q2 | q3: textual or numeric representation of the Q3 lap time as stored, derived from qualifying_attempts.q3 | position: finishing position in qualifying as stored, derived from qualifying_attempts.position
params.grounded_columns: qualifying_attempts.qualifyId | qualifying_attempts.raceId | qualifying_attempts.driverId | qualifying_attempts.q1 | qualifying_attempts.q1_milliseconds | qualifying_attempts.q2 | qualifying_attempts.q3 | qualifying_attempts.position | drivers_base.driverId | drivers_base.driverRef | drivers_base.forename | drivers_base.surname
params.metric: count_attempts = COUNT(qualifyId) -- aggregate count of qualifying attempts when grouping at a coarser grain than qualifyId | min_q1_milliseconds = MIN(q1_milliseconds) -- best (minimum) Q1 time in milliseconds when aggregated per driver or race | avg_q1_milliseconds = AVG(q1_milliseconds) -- average Q1 time in milliseconds when aggregated per driver or race | max_position = MAX(position) -- worst (maximum) position when aggregated per driver or race
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_base (or other driver dimension) on driverId — safe because this view already LEFT JOINs drivers_base and is one-row-per-qualifyId; joining to a driver dimension keyed by driverId that is one-row-per-driver will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races (or race dimension) on raceId — safe when the race dimension is one-row-per-race (one-to-one on raceId), so this view's rows and measures remain unchanged. | do NOT join directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from qualifyId (for example, a hypothetical qualifying_telemetry table keyed to qualifyId with multiple rows) without first aggregating that table to qualifyId; joining such a one-to-many table would multiply this view's rows and thereby duplicate counts/sums derived from this view. | do NOT join to tables that are one-to-many on driverId (e.g., driver_results_detail with multiple result rows per driver) unless you either (a) aggregate that table to driverId before joining, or (b) join using a strategy that preserves qualifyId uniqueness (for example, restricting to at most one matching row per qualifyId). Without such protection, aggregations like COUNT(qualifyId) or SUM(q1_milliseconds) from this view would be inflated. | When composing new metrics, aggregate at the appropriate grain: this view's native grain is qualifyId (one row per qualifying attempt). To produce driver-level metrics, GROUP BY driverId and apply aggregate functions (COUNT, MIN, AVG, etc.) on q1_milliseconds or position.

Example metric definitions are intentionally identity mappings: | driverId = drivers.driverId | driverRef = drivers.driverRef | number = drivers.number | code = drivers.code | forename = drivers.forename | surname = drivers.surname | dob = drivers.dob | nationality = drivers.nationality
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/lookup views that are also one-row-per-driver on drivers_core.driverId = <other>.driverId — safe because drivers_core is one-row-per-driver so its attributes will not be duplicated. | Examples of safe joins: | - Join to drivers_base on driverId (drivers_core.driverId = drivers_base.driverId) — both represent a single row per driver so no duplication of driver-level attributes. | - Join to qualifying_with_driver_ref on driverRef when that view is also one-row-per-driver (drivers_core.driverRef = qualifying_with_driver_ref.driverRef) — safe only if that sibling view is guaranteed unique per driverRef. | unsafe-to-join-without-reaggregation: | - Do NOT directly join drivers_core to one-to-many event/activity tables (e.g., qualifying_attempts, race_results, lap_times, pit_stops) on driverId without first aggregating the event table, because each matching event row will duplicate the driver row and thus multiply any measures derived from drivers_core. | - Specifically, do NOT join drivers_core to qualifying_attempts (one-to-many) without aggregating qualifying_attempts by driverId (e.g., COUNT(*) or other aggregation) — otherwise driver attributes will be repeated for each attempt. | recommended patterns when combining with one-to-many tables: | - Pre-aggregate the many-side by driverId (for example: SELECT driverId, COUNT(*) AS attempts FROM qualifying_attempts GROUP BY driverId) and then join that aggregated result to drivers_core on driverId — this preserves correct cardinality and prevents multiplying driver-level measures. | - Alternatively, use analytic/window functions on the many-side first and then select one row per driver before joining to drivers_core. | notes about sibling views in this DB: | - qualifying_attempts is a one-to-many (SEL) style view: do not join it directly without aggregation. | - drivers_base is a selector (SEL) sibling: verify it is one-row-per-driver before joining; safe if it is. | - qualifying_with_driver_ref is a JOIN-style sibling: confirm its cardinality per driverRef before treating it as safe to join without aggregation.

  circuitId,
  name,

  country,
  lat,

  alt,

FROM circuits

params.description: Provides one-row-per-circuit descriptive attributes (identifiers, name, geographic location and reference URL) for circuits.
params.when_to_use: Look up circuit metadata by circuitId or circuitRef | Join circuit descriptive attributes onto race-, qualifying-, or results-level datasets when you need circuit name/location/country or coordinates | Build aggregations by circuit (e.g., counts of events per circuit) by composing this view as the dimensional circuit table | Filter or map races/drivers/qualifying attempts to their circuit information
params.output_schema: circuitId: unique numeric identifier of the circuit — derived directly from circuits.circuitId | name: official circuit name — derived directly from circuits.name | location: city or locality of the circuit — derived directly from circuits.location | country: country where the circuit is located — derived directly from circuits.country | lat: latitude coordinate of the circuit — derived directly from circuits.lat | lng: longitude coordinate of the circuit — derived directly from circuits.lng | alt: altitude/elevation of the circuit (units as stored) — derived directly from circuits.alt | circuitRef: short textual reference/key for the circuit — derived directly from circuits.circuitRef | url: external URL reference for the circuit — derived directly from circuits.url
params.grounded_columns: circuits.circuitId | circuits.name | circuits.location | circuits.country | circuits.lat | circuits.lng | circuits.alt | circuits.circuitRef | circuits.url
params.metric: No derived numeric metrics in this view; all output columns are direct passthroughs of base columns | If you create metrics on top of this view, compute aggregates after joining to event/attempt/result tables; do not assume any pre-aggregated measures exist here
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact/event tables (e.g., races, qualifying_attempts, results) on circuits_core.circuitId = <fact>.circuitId — safe because circuits_core has one row per circuitId, and joining a one-row-per-circuit dimension onto many-row facts will not duplicate the circuit row (facts remain multiplicative as expected); circuits_core itself contains no aggregated measures to be accidentally duplicated. | Safe to join circuits_core to other one-row-per-circuit normalized views (if available) such as a hypothetical circuits_enriched on circuitId — safe because keys are one-to-one. | Do NOT join circuits_core to one-to-many child tables (e.g., lap_times, qualifying_attempts, races) expecting those views to remain one-row-per-circuit: such joins will produce multiple rows per circuit (multiplying downstream aggregates). If you need circuit-level aggregations after joining to a one-to-many table, either: |   - Pre-aggregate the one-to-many table to circuitId granularity (e.g., COUNT(*) AS attempts_by_circuit GROUP BY circuitId) and then join that aggregated result to circuits_core on circuitId, or |   - Join at the detailed level and then perform GROUP BY circuits_core.circuitId (and other desired circuit attributes) to compute correct circuit-level metrics. | Example safe compositions: |   - circuits_core JOIN races ON circuits_core.circuitId = races.circuitId, then GROUP BY circuits_core.circuitId to compute number of races per circuit. |   - circuits_core LEFT JOIN qualifying_attempts_agg ON circuits_core.circuitId = qualifying_attempts_agg.circuitId where qualifying_attempts_agg is pre-aggregated to one row per circuit. | Example UNSAFE direct composition without re-aggregation: |   - circuits_core JOIN qualifying_attempts ON circuits_core.circuitId = qualifying_attempts.circuitId and then selecting circuits_core.circuitId, COUNT(*) without GROUP BY circuits_core.circuitId will produce a row per qualifying_attempt and overcount if not grouped — always group or pre-aggregate.

params.output_schema: raceId: unique identifier for the race event — derived directly from races.raceId | year: season year in which the race took place — derived directly from races.year | round: championship round number for the race within that year — derived directly from races.round | circuitId: foreign key referencing the circuit that hosted the race — derived directly from races.circuitId | name: official name/title of the race — derived directly from races.name | date: race date (calendar date) — derived directly from races.date | time: race start time (as stored) — derived directly from races.time | url: reference URL for more information about the race — derived directly from races.url
params.grounded_columns: races.raceId | races.year | races.round | races.circuitId | races.name | races.date | races.time | races.url
params.metric: No derived numeric aggregates are computed in this view; all output columns are direct passthroughs from the base table. | If consumers need a race-level metric (e.g., count of qualifying attempts, number of drivers, total penalties), those metrics must be computed by aggregating over the appropriate child table (e.g., qualifying_attempts or another one-to-many table) and then joined back to this view at raceId or re-aggregated after any join that expands rows.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core on races_core.circuitId = circuits_core.circuitId — safe because circuits_core is a one-row-per-circuit dimension, so it will not duplicate races_core rows or its semantics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_core (or drivers_base) only when joining via an explicit race-level driver reference that is guaranteed one-to-one per race (NOT present in this view). By default, joining drivers_core without aggregation is unsafe because drivers are generally many-per-race. | do NOT join directly to qualifying_attempts (or qualifying_with_driver_ref) without aggregation: qualifying_attempts is one-to-many relative to races (multiple attempts per race). Joining them directly will multiply races_core rows and any race-level measures. Instead, first aggregate qualifying_attempts to race-level (e.g., COUNT(*) FILTER ... AS attempts_by_race GROUP BY raceId) and then join that aggregated result to races_core on raceId. | do NOT join to sibling JOIN views that represent many-side relationships (for example, qualifying_with_driver_ref) without first reducing them to race-level aggregates — those joins will duplicate race rows. | safe composition pattern: (1) use races_core as the driving one-row-per-race dimension; (2) LEFT JOIN one-row-per-dimension tables (circuits_core) directly; (3) for any child/many-side table (qualifying_attempts, qualifying_with_driver_ref, drivers linked via race entries), compute aggregated metrics by GROUP BY raceId and then JOIN the aggregated result to races_core on raceId so measures remain correct and not multiplied.

views.name: race_with_circuit
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.raceId AS "raceId",
  races.name AS "races.name",
  races.date AS "races.date",
  races.time AS "races.time",
  circuits.circuitId AS "circuitId",

  circuits.country AS "circuits.country"
FROM races
JOIN circuits ON races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-race details by joining races to their host circuit (race-level metadata with circuit attributes).
params.when_to_use: Look up race metadata together with the circuit where the race was held (name, date, time, circuit name, location, country). | Build race-level reporting or dashboards that need circuit attributes (e.g., list races with circuit country). | Compose into larger queries that aggregate or filter by circuit attributes while keeping race as the grain.
params.output_schema: raceId: the primary identifier of the race, derived from races.raceId | races.name: the race name/title, derived from races.name | races.date: the calendar date of the race, derived from races.date | races.time: the scheduled/local time of the race, derived from races.time | circuitId: the identifier of the circuit that hosts the race, derived from circuits.circuitId (via races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId) | circuits.name: the circuit name, derived from circuits.name | circuits.location: the circuit location (city/region), derived from circuits.location | circuits.country: the circuit country, derived from circuits.country
params.grounded_columns: races.raceId | races.name | races.date | races.time | races.circuitId | circuits.circuitId | circuits.name | circuits.location | circuits.country
params.metric: No derived numeric measures in this view. All outputs are base attributes projected from races and circuits. | If you need a race-count metric at this grain: race_count = COUNT(raceId)  -- aggregate at raceId grain (i.e., COUNT(*) over this view produces number of races).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension views that are one-to-one with circuit or race without duplicating measures: |   - Safe to join to circuits_core (or circuits_core-equivalent) on circuitId — safe because this view already contains one row per race and circuits_core is one-row-per-circuit; joining will not duplicate race-level rows as long as circuits_core is one-row-per-circuit. |   - Safe to join to races_core (or races_core-equivalent) on raceId — safe because both are one-row-per-race; joining will preserve one row per race. |   - Safe to join to drivers_core on a race-level key only if drivers_core is one-row-per-(race,driver) you intend to expand into a finer grain; if you join drivers_core without aggregation you'll multiply rows (not safe for preserving race-level measures). | Do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views that have multiple rows per race (these will duplicate race rows and any aggregate counts computed at the race grain): |   - Do NOT directly join qualifying_attempts (one-to-many per race) to this view if you intend to maintain race-level measures, unless you first aggregate qualifying_attempts up to raceId (e.g., QUAL_METRIC = COUNT(*) GROUP BY raceId) and then join on raceId. Direct join will multiply the race rows by the number of qualifying attempts per race. |   - Do NOT directly join qualifying_with_driver_ref (likely one-to-many per race) unless you aggregate it to raceId or otherwise handle the multiplicity. | Composition patterns: |   - To get race-level aggregates that include qualifying counts: pre-aggregate qualifying_attempts as (raceId, qualifying_attempts_count = COUNT(*)) and then LEFT JOIN to this view on raceId — safe because pre-aggregation ensures one row per race in the joined dataset. |   - To produce driver-level outputs (one row per race-driver), join this view to drivers_base or drivers_core on nothing (they are separate grains) only after deciding to change grain to race+driver; expect multiplication: replicate the race attributes across driver rows. | Notes on keys and uniqueness: |   - The view's grain is raceId (one row per races.raceId). The join in the view is races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId; this is safe as long as circuits.circuitId is unique in circuits (circuits is expected to be one-row-per-circuit). |   - Planner should treat the view as delivering attribute columns at the race grain. Any join that preserves raceId uniqueness (one-to-one or many-to-one into circuits) will not duplicate measures; any join that introduces multiple rows per race must be accompanied by aggregation on the many-side before joining or by changing the overall query grain and re-aggregating race-level metrics appropriately.

views.name: qualifying_with_driver_constructor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualifyId AS qualifyId,
  q.raceId AS raceId,
  q.driverId AS driverId,
  d.forename AS driver_forename,
  d.surname AS driver_surname,
  d.number AS driver_number,
  q.constructorId AS constructorId,
  c.name AS constructor_name,
  q.number AS number,
  q.q1 AS q1,
  q.q2 AS q2,
  q.q3 AS q3,

FROM qualifying q

params.description: A denormalized qualifying row per qualifyId that includes the linked driver and constructor attributes (forename, surname, numbers, constructor name) and the three qualifying session times and grid position.
params.when_to_use: Report or query needing qualifying session results at the qualifyId (one qualifying entry) grain including driver and constructor attributes. | Compose race weekend summaries that compare qualifying times or positions across drivers/constructors. | Filter or join qualifying results to races, drivers, constructors, or circuits while preserving one row per qualifying entry. | Build aggregates such as best Q1/Q2/Q3 times per driver/constructor or counts of qualifying appearances (must aggregate after joining any one-to-many).

params.grounded_columns: qualifying.qualifyId | qualifying.raceId | qualifying.driverId | qualifying.constructorId | qualifying.number | qualifying.q1 | qualifying.q2 | qualifying.q3 | qualifying.position | drivers.driverId | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.number | constructors.constructorId | constructors.name
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated measures; all columns are direct passthroughs. If you need aggregates, compute them over this view while respecting its grain (qualifyId). | Example derived metrics you can compute safely on this view: count_qualify_entries = COUNT(qualifyId), best_q1_time = MIN(q1) (ensure q1 is non-null and numeric), avg_q1_time = AVG(q1). These must be computed by the consuming query.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races_core (or race_with_circuit) on raceId = races_core.raceId — safe because this view is one-row-per-qualifyId and raceId is a many-to-one relationship from qualify entries to race; joining to race (one row per race) will not duplicate qualifying rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_core or drivers_base on driverId = drivers_core.driverId — safe because each qualifying row references a single driver row (drivers are one per driverId). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructors (constructors_core if present) on constructorId = constructors.constructorId — safe because each qualifying row references a single constructor row. | DO NOT join without aggregation to any table/view that is one-to-many from a qualifying entry (i.e., that has multiple rows per qualifyId or per driverId within the same race) because it will multiply these qualifying rows and therefore duplicate any measures derived at qualifyId grain. For example, do NOT directly join to a hypothetical lap_times table keyed by driverId+raceId (many laps per qualifying entry) unless you first aggregate laps to the qualifyId grain (e.g., MIN(lap_time) per qualifyId) or use DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER logic to keep one row per qualifyId. | If you need driver- or constructor-level aggregates for downstream joins (e.g., total podiums per driver), pre-aggregate that other dataset to driverId (one row per driverId) before joining to this view to avoid duplicating qualifying rows. | When composing multi-grain queries (e.g., race-level summaries from this qualify-level view), always re-aggregate qualifying measures to the desired target grain (raceId, driverId, constructorId) after joining any additional dimensions that are many-to-one with respect to the chosen aggregation key.

params.grounded_columns: races.raceId | races.year | races.name | races.round | races.circuitId | races.date | races.time
params.metric: No aggregate metrics are defined in this view; all output columns are direct projections from base table columns. | If you need derived metrics at the race grain, compute them in an aggregation over a one-to-many child table keyed by raceId (e.g., COUNT(*) over results WHERE results.raceId = race_rows.raceId). Example pattern: participants_count = COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE <participant criteria>) GROUP BY raceId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races_core (or races_core/NORM siblings) on raceId — safe because race_rows is one-row-per-race (raceId is unique here) so joining a race-level dimension does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core or circuits_core_7 on circuitId = race_rows.circuitId — safe because those circuit dimension views are one-row-per-circuit; joining attaches circuit attributes without duplicating race rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_with_circuit on raceId = race_rows.raceId — safe when race_with_circuit is also one-row-per-race; verify sibling view semantics before joining but typically safe. | do NOT directly join to one-to-many child tables/views such as qualifying_attempts, qualifying_with_driver_ref, qualifying_with_driver_constructor, qualifying_attempts, drivers_base (if used as multiple drivers per race), or race_qualifying_cohort without aggregation — those joins would multiply the race_rows rows and therefore multiply any race-level measures. Joining will not duplicate result-level measures since race_results is one-row-per-resultId and drivers_core is one-row-per-driver. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races_core (or race_rows / race_with_circuit) on raceId — safe because races_core is one-row-per-race; joining will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (via race_with_circuit) on raceId -> race_with_circuit.raceId -> circuits_core.circuitId — safe when joining race_results -> race_with_circuit (on raceId) then to circuits_core (on circuitId) because race_with_circuit is one-row-per-race and circuits_core is one-row-per-circuit; the path preserves one result row per resultId. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to qualifying_with_driver_ref or qualifying_with_driver_constructor on (raceId, driverId) only if those views are one-row-per-(raceId,driverId) qualifying record; confirm sibling view grain before joining. If qualifying views are one-row-per-attempt, they will multiply rows and must be aggregated first (e.g., best lap) before joining. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many detail without aggregation: for example, do NOT join race_results to a table/view that has multiple rows per resultId (there are no such tables referenced here, but sibling 'qualifying_attempts' is likely one-to-many per (raceId,driverId) — joining it directly will multiply points/grid/time measures). views.name: result_with_driver_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.resultId AS resultId,
  results.raceId AS raceId,
  results.driverId AS driverId,
  drivers.forename AS forename,
  drivers.surname AS surname,
  drivers.nationality AS nationality,
  results.fastestLapSpeed AS fastestLapSpeed_raw,
  -- parse numeric part: try to cast directly; if contains non-numeric characters, remove non-digit/dot via simple approach

  CASE
    WHEN trim(results.fastestLapSpeed) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN (results.fastestLapSpeed GLOB '*[0-9]*') = 0 THEN NULL

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_core (or drivers_base/drivers_core variants) on driverId = drivers_core.driverId — safe because drivers_core is one-row-per-driver and joining to it will not duplicate result rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races_core (or race_rows/race_with_circuit) on raceId = races_core.raceId — safe because races_core is one-row-per-race and will not duplicate result rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (via race -> circuit through race_with_circuit) only if you join races first (raceId -> races_core, then races_core.circuitId -> circuits_core) — safe because each intermediate join is one-to-one from result -> race -> circuit. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as qualifying_attempts or qualifying_with_driver_constructor without re-aggregation first because those are many rows per result or per driver and would multiply result-level measures (e.g., points) unless you aggregate the many-side (e.g., MAX/ROW_NUMBER filter) before joining. | If you need to bring qualifying_attempts data into result-level rows, first aggregate qualifying_attempts to one row per driver+race (for example MIN(lapTime) or QUAL_POS using ROW_NUMBER) and then join on (raceId, driverId) so this view's per-result measures remain correct. | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., total points per driver), aggregate result-level points (SUM(points)) grouping by driverId after joining any dimensions — do not sum across a result-level table that has been duplicated by a many-side join without re-aggregation.

views.name: results_fastest_lap_speed_numeric
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  r.fastestLapSpeed,
  CASE
    WHEN r.fastestLapSpeed IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE (
      -- remove any non-digit, non-dot, non-minus characters and collapse multiple dots
      -- Step 1: remove spaces
      -- Step 2: keep only digits, dot, minus using nested REPLACE and LIKE checks since SQLite lacks regex replace
      -- We'll iteratively strip common non-numeric characters: letters, plus signs, commas, and percent signs
      -- Start from raw text
      (CASE
        WHEN trim(replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(r.fastestLapSpeed, ' ', ''), ',', ''), '+', ''), '%', ''), 'kph', '')) = '' THEN NULL
        ELSE
          -- If the cleaned string looks like a plain numeric value, cast to real, else NULL
          (CASE
            WHEN trim(
              replace(
                replace(
                  replace(
                    replace(
                      replace(
                        replace(
                          replace(
                            replace(r.fastestLapSpeed, ' ', ''),
                          ',', ''),
                        '+', ''),
                      '%', ''),
                    'kph', ''),
                  'KPH', ''),
                'km/h', ''),
              'Km/h', '')
            ) GLOB '-[0-9]*.*' OR trim(
              replace(
                replace(
                  replace(
                    replace(
                      replace(
                        replace(
                          replace(
                            replace(r.fastestLapSpeed, ' ', ''),
                          ',', ''),
                        '+', ''),
                      '%', ''),
                    'kph', ''),
                  'KPH', ''),
                'km/h', ''),
              'Km/h', '')
            ) GLOB '[0-9]*.*' THEN CAST(
              trim(
                replace(
                  replace(
                    replace(
                      replace(
                        replace(
                          replace(
                            replace(
                              replace(r.fastestLapSpeed, ' ', ''),
                            ',', ''),
                          '+', ''),
                        '%', ''),
                      'kph', ''),
                    'KPH', ''),
                  'km/h', ''),
                'Km/h', '')
              ) AS REAL)
            ELSE NULL
          END)
      END)
    )
  END AS fastestLapSpeed_num
FROM results r

params.description: Provides one row per race result with the original fastest lap speed text and a cleaned numeric version suitable for numeric comparisons and aggregation.
params.when_to_use: You need the fastest lap speed for a given result as a numeric value (e.g., sorting, averaging, filtering by speed). | Composing queries that join result-level metrics (fastest lap speed) to driver, race, or qualifying data without duplicating measures. | Cleaning and normalizing raw fastestLapSpeed text into a numeric column for downstream analysis or visualizations.
params.output_schema: resultId: unique identifier of the race result row — derives from results.resultId | raceId: identifier of the race for this result — derives from results.raceId | driverId: identifier of the driver for this result — derives from results.driverId | fastestLapSpeed: original raw text value of the fastest lap speed as stored in results.fastestLapSpeed | fastestLapSpeed_num: cleaned numeric (REAL) version of fastestLapSpeed; NULL when the raw value is NULL or cannot be parsed. Derived by removing common non-numeric tokens (spaces, commas, +, %, unit strings like 'kph', 'KPH', 'km/h', ...) and then casting to a numeric type when the cleaned string matches a numeric pattern.
params.grounded_columns: results.resultId | results.raceId | results.driverId | results.fastestLapSpeed
params.metric: fastestLapSpeed_num = CASE WHEN results.fastestLapSpeed IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE (clean-and-parse-expression) END | Where (clean-and-parse-expression) is implemented as iterative REPLACE/TRIM operations that strip spaces, commas, plus signs, percent signs, and common unit suffixes (e.g., 'kph','KPH','km/h','Km/h'), returning NULL if the cleaned string is empty or does not match a numeric glob pattern; otherwise CAST(cleaned_string AS REAL).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE joins: join to driver-level or race-level one-row-per-entity views/tables without duplicating this view's measures: |   - Join to drivers_core (or drivers_base) on driverId — safe because drivers_core is one-row-per-driver so joining will attach driver attributes to each result row without duplicating result-level measures. |   - Join to races_core (or race_rows) on raceId — safe because races_core is one-row-per-race so each result row remains one row and measures (fastestLapSpeed_num) are not multiplied. |   - Join to circuits_core via race -> circuit (e.g., via race_with_circuit or races_core.raceId->circuits) only if you join on a one-row-per-race or one-row-per-circuit key; joining race_with_circuit on raceId is safe when race_with_circuit is one-row-per-race. |  | joins that are NOT safe without aggregation or de-duplication (these will duplicate result-level numeric measures and must be handled carefully): |   - Do NOT join this view directly to any table/view that is one-to-many from results (for example, any lap-level, pit-stop-level, or qualifying-attempts-per-result tables) without first aggregating those many-rows back to a single row per resultId. Such joins will multiply rows for a single resultId and therefore multiply fastestLapSpeed_num incorrectly. |   - Do NOT join directly to qualifying_attempts or other attempt-level views that contain multiple rows per resultId/driverId unless you aggregate (e.g., MAX, MIN, AVG) the attempt-level rows grouped by resultId before joining. |  | general guidance for safe composition: |   - Preserve the resultId grain: any join that remains at one-row-per-resultId (e.g., one-to-one or many-to-one into results by resultId, driverId, or raceId) keeps fastestLapSpeed_num safe to use directly in aggregates (SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX) computed after the join. |   - If you must join a one-to-many dimension, either (a) aggregate the many-side to one row per resultId before joining, or (b) use window functions / distinct-aggregates keyed by resultId to avoid duplicating measures. |   - When composing further measures that aggregate fastestLapSpeed_num (e.g., average fastest lap speed per driver or per race), group by the desired key (driverId or raceId) and aggregate fastestLapSpeed_num in the expected way; do not rely on row counts from joined many-side tables.

views.name: results_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  resultId,
  raceId,
  driverId,
  constructorId,
  grid,
  position,
  positionText,
  positionOrder,
  points,
  laps,
  time,
  milliseconds,
  statusId
FROM results

params.description: One-row-per-result (race entry) facts: the finishing/result data for each driver in a race.
params.when_to_use: Get the result record for a specific resultId or list of resultIds. | List all results for a given raceId (all drivers' finishing positions and points). | Aggregate driver or constructor season totals by composing/aggregating points, laps, or counts from this view. | Join result-level details to driver, constructor, race or circuit dimensions to build richer reports (pace, finishing status, standings). | Serve as the base granular fact when computing per-result metrics (e.g., points per result, finished_count) before further aggregation.
params.output_schema: resultId: unique identifier for this result row — derived directly from results.resultId | raceId: identifier of the race this result belongs to — derived directly from results.raceId | driverId: identifier of the driver for this result — derived directly from results.driverId | constructorId: identifier of the constructor/team for this result — derived directly from results.constructorId | grid: starting grid position for this result (numeric) — derived directly from results.grid | position: finishing position as stored (may be NULL or textual number) — derived directly from results.position | positionText: finishing position text (e.g., 'DNF') — derived directly from results.positionText | positionOrder: numeric finishing order used for ordering/aggregation — derived directly from results.positionOrder | points: points awarded for this result (numeric, can be fractional) — derived directly from results.points | laps: number of laps completed by this result (numeric) — derived directly from results.laps | time: finishing time as stored (string) — derived directly from results.time | milliseconds: finishing time in milliseconds (numeric) — derived directly from results.milliseconds | statusId: status identifier for the result (references results.statusId) — derived directly from results.statusId
params.grounded_columns: results.resultId | results.raceId | results.driverId | results.constructorId | results.grid | results.position | results.positionText | results.positionOrder | results.points | results.laps | results.time | results.milliseconds | results.statusId
params.metric: points = results.points (atomic measure at the result row grain; to compute totals use SUM(points) grouped at the desired grain) | laps = results.laps (atomic measure at the result row grain; aggregate with SUM(laps) for total laps by driver/race/season) | result_count = COUNT(resultId) (derived cardinality metric: count of result rows in a group) | finished_count = SUM(CASE WHEN positionOrder IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) (example derived metric to count classified finishes — must be computed by the planner on top of this view) | total_milliseconds = SUM(milliseconds) (aggregate over results to get cumulative race time; NULLs should be handled according to desired semantics)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_core (or drivers_base, drivers_core) on results.driverId = drivers_core.driverId — safe because results_rows is one-row-per-result and drivers_core is one-row-per-driver; joining adds driver attributes without duplicating result measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races_core (or race_rows, race_with_circuit) on results.raceId = races_core.raceId — safe because races_core is one-row-per-race; result-level measures remain one-per-result. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (via race_with_circuit -> races_core.raceId join) on race -> circuit keys — safe when joining races (1 race -> 1 circuit), so results keep one row per result. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to qualifying_with_driver_constructor or qualifying_with_driver_ref on (raceId, driverId) when those sibling views are one-row-per-(race,driver) qualifying attempt — safe only if the qualifying view is guaranteed to be at most one row per (raceId, driverId). Verify sibling view grain before joining. | do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views such as qualifying_attempts (which may have multiple attempts per driver per race) directly to this view on (raceId, driverId) because that will multiply result rows and therefore duplicate measures like points and laps; instead, pre-aggregate the many-side (e.g., take MAX/ MIN / FIRST / aggregate) to one-row-per-(raceId,driverId) before joining. | do NOT join directly to any event-level or telemetry tables that have multiple rows per result (e.g., lap_times, pit_stops if present) unless you aggregate those tables first (e.g., SUM, COUNT, AVG) grouped by the result's key (raceId, driverId or resultId) to avoid inflating the result-level measures. | If you need to bring in many-side detail (multiple rows) for analytical exploration, keep the join but then always re-aggregate the combined set back to the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY resultId and use SUM/AVG on metrics) to restore correct measure semantics.

views.name: races_core_33
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  raceId,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  strftime('%Y', date) AS year_text,
  strftime('%m', date) AS month_text,
  circuitId
FROM races

params.description: One-row-per-race canonical row with basic race attributes (identifiers, name, date/time, year/month text, and circuit reference).
params.when_to_use: List or lookup of races with their date/time and associated circuit | Filtering or grouping races by year_text or month_text | Joining race-level attributes to other race-level metrics (e.g., results, qualifying aggregates) without duplicating race rows | As the foundation for building race-level aggregates or for joining to dimension tables that are 1:1 with race
params.output_schema: raceId: unique race identifier (derived directly from races.raceId) | name: race name/title (derived directly from races.name) | date: race date (derived directly from races.date) | time: race start time (derived directly from races.time) | year_text: 4-digit year as text, extracted from races.date via strftime('%Y', date) | month_text: 2-digit month as text, extracted from races.date via strftime('%m', date) | circuitId: foreign key referencing the circuit for the race (derived directly from races.circuitId)
params.grounded_columns: races.raceId | races.name | races.date | races.time | races.circuitId
params.metric: year_text = strftime('%Y', races.date) | month_text = strftime('%m', races.date)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (or circuits_core_7 or race_with_circuit) on races_core_33.circuitId = circuits_core.circuitId — safe because races_core_33 is one-row-per-race (grain = raceId) and circuits is one-row-per-circuit; joining a race to its circuit does not duplicate race-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_core on a driver-key only if the join is known to be 1:1 for the intended analysis (rare). Prefer joining via an intermediate one-row-per-race-per-driver view (e.g., race_results aggregated to one row per race-driver) to avoid duplication. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many race-level detail tables/views (for example: race_results, qualifying_attempts, qualifying_with_driver_ref, qualifying_with_driver_constructor, race_rows, race_qualifying_cohort) without aggregation or deduplication first — these are one-to-many from race to rows and will multiply race rows and any derived race-level metrics. | When composing aggregates: if you need race-level measures derived from many rows (for example, count of qualifying attempts, count of results, sums), first aggregate the child table to one row per raceId (or otherwise produce one row per raceId) and then join to races_core_33 on raceId. This preserves the one-row-per-race cardinality and avoids measure inflation. | If joining to sibling JOIN views that already produce one row per raceId (verify their grain), those joins are safe — always confirm the target view's grain before composing.

views.name: races_by_year_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(r.year AS TEXT) AS year_text,
  CAST(STRFTIME('%m', r.date) AS TEXT) AS month_text,
  COUNT(r.raceId) AS race_count,
  MIN(r.date) AS earliest_date_in_period
FROM races r
WHERE r.date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(r.year AS TEXT), STRFTIME('%m', r.date)

params.description: Counts of races per calendar year and month (YYYY, MM) and the earliest race date in each year-month period.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of races that occurred in each year-month (e.g., trend analysis by month within years). | As a base aggregated timeseries to join to dimensions (circuits, drivers, seasons) for reporting without recounting race rows. | Compose higher-level metrics per year-month (e.g., rates, averages) by joining other aggregated measures at the same year-month grain.
params.output_schema: year_text: the race year cast to text, derived from races.year (CAST(r.year AS TEXT) AS year_text) | month_text: two-digit month string ('01'..'12') derived from STRFTIME('%m', races.date) (CAST(STRFTIME('%m', r.date) AS TEXT) AS month_text) | race_count: integer count of races in that year-month, derived from COUNT(r.raceId) | earliest_date_in_period: the minimum races.date in that year-month, derived from MIN(r.date)
params.grounded_columns: races.year | races.date | races.raceId
params.metric: race_count = COUNT(races.raceId)  -- aggregate count of raceId for the group (year_text, month_text) | earliest_date_in_period = MIN(races.date)  -- minimum calendar date in the group
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like one-row-per-key views/tables on (year_text, month_text) — for example, a calendar/date-dimension that has one row per year-month. This is safe because races_by_year_month already has one row per (year_text, month_text) so joining a one-to-one or many-to-one dimension will not duplicate race_count. | Do NOT join directly to a table or view that is one-to-many with respect to (year_text, month_text) without re-aggregating the other table to (year_text, month_text) first. Examples of unsafe joins: joining to race_results, qualifying_attempts, or any per-race/per-session detail that has multiple rows per race or per month — these will multiply race_count and other aggregates. Instead, aggregate those detail tables to the same (year_text, month_text) grain before joining (e.g., SUM, COUNT, AVG grouped by the same year_text and month_text expressions). | If you need to enrich this view with per-race dimensions (e.g., circuits or drivers), join via a pre-aggregated or distinct list of race identifiers per year-month. For example: derive a set of raceId -> year_text/month_text from races (or from races_by_year_month join back to races on year/date) and then join de-duplicated race-level attributes, or aggregate the attribute at the year-month level before combining with this view. | This view's measures are computed at the group (year_text, month_text). Any join that preserves one row per (year_text, month_text) is safe. Any join that introduces multiple rows per (year_text, month_text) requires re-aggregation (e.g., wrap the joined result in GROUP BY year_text, month_text and recompute SUM(race_count) or other appropriate aggregates).

views.name: results_with_driver_dims
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  r.points
FROM results r
JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = r.driverId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-result details: result identifiers, associated race and driver identifiers, driver name, and points earned for that result.
params.when_to_use: Lookup the driver and race for a specific resultId or set of resultIds. | Report points scored by drivers in specific races or results. | Join driver name and basic driver identifiers onto result-level analyses or aggregations. | Compose further aggregations at the result grain (for example: sum points by driver or by race) without risking double-counting, provided downstream joins preserve the result-level cardinality or re-aggregate appropriately.
params.output_schema: resultId: Unique identifier for the race result row — derived from results.resultId | raceId: Identifier of the race associated with the result — derived from results.raceId | driverId: Identifier of the driver who produced the result — derived from results.driverId | forename: Driver forename (given name) — derived from drivers.forename | surname: Driver surname (family name) — derived from drivers.surname | points: Points awarded for this result — derived from results.points
params.grounded_columns: results.resultId | results.raceId | results.driverId | results.points | drivers.driverId | drivers.forename | drivers.surname
params.metric: points = results.points  -- atomic measure at the resultId grain (no aggregation applied in this view). | When aggregated: sum(points) by driverId = total points across results for that driver (requires grouping by driverId). | When aggregated: sum(points) by raceId = total points awarded in that race (requires grouping by raceId).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver-level dimension views (e.g., drivers_core, drivers_base, drivers_core_7) on driverId — safe because drivers are one row per driver and this view is one row per result; joining driver dimension will not duplicate results' points, since each result.driverId maps to a single driver row. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race-level or race-with-circuit views (e.g., races_core, race_with_circuit, race_rows) on raceId — safe because races are one row per race and this view is one row per result; joining race dimension will not duplicate this view's measures. | DO NOT join this view directly to one-to-many detail tables or views (for example: qualifying_attempts, qualifying_with_driver_ref, qualifying_with_driver_constructor, race_qualifying_cohort, or any other view that contains multiple rows per resultId or per (raceId, driverId)) without first re-aggregating the detail to the resultId (or to the desired grain). Such joins would multiply rows and thus duplicate the points measure. If you need metrics from a one-to-many source, either: |   - aggregate the one-to-many source up to resultId (or to the grain you intend) before joining, or |   - join and then re-aggregate the combined set back to the intended grain (e.g., group by resultId or driverId and SUM(points) after the join). | If composing with sibling view race_results (JOIN) ensure you join on the appropriate key: if race_results is one row per resultId, join on resultId is safe; if race_results is at a different grain, re-aggregate before joining. | Example safe composition patterns: |   - To compute total points per driver: SELECT driverId, SUM(points) FROM results_with_driver_dims GROUP BY driverId — or join drivers_core on driverId to add driver attributes, still safe. |   - To add circuit attributes: join results_with_driver_dims -> race_with_circuit (on raceId) -> circuits_core (on circuitId) because race_with_circuit and circuits_core are one-row-per-race / one-row-per-circuit respectively. | Example unsafe composition patterns (avoid without aggregation): |   - results_with_driver_dims JOIN qualifying_attempts ON results_with_driver_dims.resultId = qualifying_attempts.resultId  -- unsafe if qualifying_attempts has multiple rows per resultId (will duplicate points). |   - results_with_driver_dims JOIN qualifying_with_driver_ref ON driverId = driverId (if qualifying_with_driver_ref is many-per-driver) — will duplicate result rows unless qualifying_with_driver_ref is aggregated to driverId first.

  raceId,
  driverId,
  lap,
  time,
  milliseconds
FROM lapTimes

params.description: Row-level lap time records: one row per raceId, driverId, lap with lap time text and milliseconds value.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve individual lap times for a driver in a specific race or across races | Compute aggregates over laps (e.g., average lap time per driver/race) by aggregating this view | Filter or join to dimensional data (driver, race, circuit) while preserving per-lap granularity | Drive lap-level analytics such as fastest lap detection, stint segmentation (when combined with additional data), or lap-by-lap progression charts
params.output_schema: raceId: race identifier (derives from lapTimes.raceId) | driverId: driver identifier (derives from lapTimes.driverId) | lap: lap number within the race (derives from lapTimes.lap) | time: lap time as recorded text/string (derives from lapTimes.time) | milliseconds: lap time in milliseconds as integer (derives from lapTimes.milliseconds)
params.grounded_columns: lapTimes.raceId | lapTimes.driverId | lapTimes.lap | lapTimes.time | lapTimes.milliseconds
params.metric: milliseconds = lapTimes.milliseconds  -- atomic numeric measure (per-row, not aggregated) | count_rows = COUNT(*) when aggregated over this view (not present as a column; use SQL aggregation to compute)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_core (or drivers_base) on drivers_core.driverId = lap_times_rowlevel.driverId — safe because lap_times_rowlevel is one-row-per (raceId, driverId, lap); joining to a one-row-per-driver dimension will not duplicate lap-level rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races_core (or race_rows, race_with_circuit) on races_core.raceId = lap_times_rowlevel.raceId — safe because races_core is one-row-per-race and thus does not multiply lap rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (or race_with_circuit -> circuits_core via raceId) by first joining races_core (raceId) then circuits_core on circuitId = races_core.circuitId — safe when the circuit side is one-row-per-circuit. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., race_results, qualifying_attempts, qualifying_with_driver_constructor) without aggregation because those joins can multiply lap rows: for example, joining lap_times_rowlevel to race_results on (raceId, driverId) is dangerous if race_results contains multiple result rows per (raceId, driverId) because it will duplicate milliseconds and other per-lap measures. | If you must combine with a one-to-many sibling (qualifying_attempts, race_results, qualifying_with_driver_ref, qualifying_with_driver_constructor), either: (a) aggregate the one-to-many table to one row per the join key before joining (e.g., SUM/AVG/COUNT over its rows grouped by raceId, driverId), or (b) aggregate lap_times_rowlevel after the join to re-compute intended measures at the desired grain. | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., avg_milliseconds_per_driver_per_race), compute them by aggregating milliseconds from this view grouped by raceId and driverId to avoid double-counting from subsequent joins.

LEFT JOIN driverStandings ds

NULL if driver has no standings rows. | standings_row_count: count of driverStandings rows joined for that driver; derived from COUNT(ds.driverStandingsId). Returns 0 when no matching driverStandings rows exist because of LEFT JOIN? (Note: COUNT on driverStandingsId yields 0 only when no non-null ids exist; due to LEFT JOIN it will be 0 for drivers with no standings rows.)

a naive join would multiply rows and thus over-count total_wins and standings_row_count and distort max_points. | do NOT join directly to race_results or race_rows or any table that contains multiple rows per driver (e.g., per race) without re-aggregating after the join or performing the join from the many-side into this aggregated driver-level view using a DISTINCT/aggregation, because those joins can duplicate this view's measures. | If you need driver-level aggregates combined with another many-to-one dimension (for example, to compute per-team sums of driver total_wins), first aggregate the many-side to driverId (or aggregate this view's measures after joining but using SUM(...) with GROUP BY team), or join this view (one-row-per-driver) to a team mapping that is 1:1 on driverId — safe only if the team mapping is 1:1. | When composing into larger aggregations (e.g., team-level totals), treat total_wins and standings_row_count as additive metrics (SUM over drivers is correct), but treat max_points as a per-driver maximum; to compute team-level max_points you must take MAX(max_points) after grouping by team (NOT SUM). | If joining to sibling JOIN views that already expand driver rows (for example qualifying_with_driver_ref or qualifying_with_driver_constructor), ensure those views are reduced to one row per driver before combining with this view, or aggregate the combined result to driverId to avoid duplicating aggregated measures.

  d.forename AS forename,

Example safe pattern: (SELECT driverId, SUM(points) AS total_points FROM race_results GROUP BY driverId) AS drv_points JOIN drivers_base_44 USING(driverId). | Avoid joining in a way that relies on this view to carry multiplicative metrics (it contains no aggregated measures beyond current_age_years which is computed per row). views.name: driver_age_metrics_by_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driverId,
  d.dob,
  CAST((julianday('now') - julianday(d.dob)) / 365.2425 AS INTEGER) AS age_years,
  CAST((julianday('now') - julianday(d.dob)) AS INTEGER) AS age_days
FROM drivers d
WHERE d.dob IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY d.driverId, d.dob

params.description: Per-driver age metrics (age in years and age in days) calculated from each driver's date of birth.
params.when_to_use: Show or filter drivers by current age (years or days). | Join driver demographic age information into driver-level analyses (e.g., join to driver performance, qualifying, or results aggregated at driver level). | Build cohorts or buckets based on driver age for further aggregation (e.g., count drivers by age group, average results by age).
params.output_schema: driverId: unique identifier for the driver — sourced from drivers.driverId | dob: driver date of birth (date) — sourced from drivers.dob | age_years: integer age in years computed as floor((today - dob) / 365.2425) — derived from julianday('now') - julianday(drivers.dob) and cast to INTEGER in the view SQL | age_days: integer age in days computed as floor(today - dob) — derived from julianday('now') - julianday(drivers.dob) and cast to INTEGER in the view SQL
params.grounded_columns: drivers.driverId | drivers.dob
params.metric: age_years = CAST((julianday('now') - julianday(drivers.dob)) / 365.2425 AS INTEGER)  -- integer years since dob (uses 365.2425 to approximate Gregorian year) | age_days = CAST((julianday('now') - julianday(drivers.dob)) AS INTEGER)  -- integer days since dob
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver-level dimensions or views that are 1:1 with drivers on driverId — e.g., drivers_core (JOIN ON drivers_core.driverId = driver_age_metrics_by_driver.driverId) — safe because driver_age_metrics_by_driver is one row per driverId (grain: driverId, dob) and joining to another one-row-per-driver view will not duplicate rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver-level selects such as drivers_base or drivers_core_7 on driverId — safe for the same reason (both are one-row-per-driver). | NOT safe to directly join to one-to-many tables/views (without re-aggregation) such as qualifying_attempts, qualifying_with_driver_ref, qualifying_with_driver_constructor, race_results, race_rows, or any race/qualifying event tables on driverId — these are many rows per driver and would duplicate driver_age_metrics_by_driver rows and thus multiply its measures. | If you need driver age metrics in analyses that join to one-to-many event tables, either: (a) aggregate the event-side rows to driver-level first (so both sides are one-row-per-driver) and then join, or (b) join and then re-aggregate after the join, ensuring you do not SUM or COUNT age_years/age_days directly (age fields are attributes, not additive measures). For example, compute AVG(age_years) over drivers by aggregating driver_age_metrics_by_driver grouped by whatever cohort keys before joining to events, or join events to drivers and use MAX(age_years) or ANY_VALUE(age_years) when re-aggregating to avoid duplication. | Do NOT treat age_years or age_days as additive metrics to be summed across joined event rows; they are attributes/derived columns representing each driver's age. Use non-additive aggregations (MIN, MAX, AVG) or pre-aggregate to driver grain.

views.name: races_with_circuits
views.body_sql:
SELECT

  races.name AS race_name,
  circuits.name AS circuit_name,
  circuits.location AS circuit_location,
  races.circuitId AS circuitId
FROM races
JOIN circuits ON races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-race details including race and its circuit's name and location.
params.when_to_use: Look up race-level descriptive attributes (race name, circuit name, circuit location) for reporting or display. | Start a query that needs race-level context alongside other race-keyed metrics (e.g., counts or aggregates per race). | Join race descriptive metadata into race-level aggregates (e.g., qualifying counts, result summaries) while preserving race grain.
params.output_schema: race_name: The race's display name — derived from races.name. | circuit_name: The circuit's display name for the race — derived from circuits.name. | circuit_location: The circuit's location (city/country/etc.) for the race — derived from circuits.location. | raceId: The primary key identifying the race (one row per race) — derived from races.raceId. | circuitId: The foreign key on races pointing to circuits.circuitId — derived from races.circuitId.
params.grounded_columns: races.raceId | races.name | races.circuitId | circuits.circuitId | circuits.name | circuits.location
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All columns are passthrough attributes at the race grain. (If you need counts or other aggregates, compute them in a separate aggregation over a one-to-many child and then join or join-then-aggregate as described in composition.)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensions or views that are one-row-per-race on raceId — e.g., join to race_rows or races_core (if available) on raceId — safe because races_with_circuits is one-row-per-race (driven by races.raceId) so measures in this view are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (or circuits_core_7) on circuitId — safe because circuits is one-row-per-circuit; joining on circuitId preserves one-row-per-race (each race references exactly one circuit row) so this view's race grain is maintained. | Do NOT join unchecked to one-to-many child tables/views (examples in this DB: qualifying_attempts, qualifying_with_driver_ref, qualifying_with_driver_constructor, race_results, race_qualifying_cohort) directly without aggregation, because those are many rows per race and would duplicate the race rows and any race-level measures. Instead, either: | - pre-aggregate the child to race-level (e.g., SELECT raceId, COUNT(*) AS attempts_count FROM qualifying_attempts GROUP BY raceId) and then join the aggregated result to this view on raceId; or | - join the child and then re-aggregate at race grain (e.g., GROUP BY races_with_circuits.raceId) to remove duplication. | When composing with other one-row-per-entity normalized views (drivers_core, circuits_core, races_core), prefer joining on their primary keys (driverId, circuitId, raceId) because these joins are 1:1 or many-to-1 from the perspective of this view and will not multiply rows. | If you must join to a sibling JOIN view (e.g., race_results) that contains aggregated race-level measures and is known to be one-row-per-race, verify its grain before joining; only join directly if it is also one-row-per-race to avoid multiplication. | When building further SELECTs on top of this view, treat raceId as the canonical grain key. Any derived metrics added above should be explicitly defined as aggregates grouped by raceId to keep semantics clear.

views.name: results_per_race_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  r.constructorId,
  r.position,
  r.positionText,
  r.positionOrder,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.statusId
FROM results r

params.description: Per-race, per-driver race result details (one row per result), i.e. the result record for a single driver in a single race.
params.when_to_use: Report or query that needs the result record for a specific driver in a specific race (positions, points, laps, time, status). | Compose driver-season or race-level aggregates by grouping/aggregating these per-driver-per-race rows (e.g., total points per driver, average finish position). | Join with driver, constructor, race or circuit dimensions to add descriptive attributes while preserving correct cardinality when aggregated from this grain. | Filter analyses to a subset of results (e.g., only classified finishes, only top-3 positions) before further aggregation.
params.output_schema: raceId: identifier of the race that this result belongs to (derived from results.raceId). | driverId: identifier of the driver who achieved this result (derived from results.driverId). | position: textual/nullable finishing position as stored (derived from results.position). | positionText: finishing position text as stored (derived from results.positionText). | positionOrder: numeric ordering of finishing position used for sorting (derived from results.positionOrder). | points: points awarded to the driver for this result (derived from results.points). | laps: number of laps completed by the driver in this race result (derived from results.laps). | time: human-readable race time/duration string for this result (derived from results.time). | milliseconds: race time in milliseconds for this result (derived from results.milliseconds). | statusId: identifier of the result status (e.g., finished, retired) (derived from results.statusId). | constructorId: identifier of the constructor/team associated with this result (derived from results.constructorId). | resultId: primary identifier of this result record (derived from results.resultId).
params.grounded_columns: results.resultId | results.raceId | results.driverId | results.constructorId | results.position | results.positionText | results.positionOrder | results.points | results.laps | results.time | results.milliseconds | results.statusId
params.metric: points = results.points (atomic numeric measure; to aggregate total points sum(points) after grouping by desired dimension) | laps = results.laps (atomic numeric measure; to aggregate total laps sum(laps)) | milliseconds = results.milliseconds (atomic numeric measure; to aggregate total/avg time sum(milliseconds)/avg(milliseconds)) | positionOrder = results.positionOrder (ordering/sort key; not an aggregate by itself; use min()/max()/avg() as needed) | position (and positionText) = stored attributes (categorical/textual measures; typically used in filters or as group-by)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_core (or drivers_base / drivers_core-like dimension) on results_per_race_driver.driverId = drivers_core.driverId — safe because results_per_race_driver is one-row-per (raceId, driverId) and drivers_core is one-row-per driver, so driver attributes enrich each result without duplicating result-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races_core (or race_rows / race_with_circuit) on results_per_race_driver.raceId = races_core.raceId — safe because races_core is one-row-per race and will not duplicate this view's measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (or race_with_circuit -> circuits) by first joining races_core to circuits (one-to-one via raceId->circuitId) and then to results_per_race_driver via raceId — safe if the race->circuit join is one-to-one; do not directly assume circuits_core joins to results without going through races to preserve cardinality. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to qualifying_with_driver_ref or qualifying_attempts on (raceId, driverId) to combine result rows with the driver's qualifying attempts for the same race — safe when qualifying views are one-row-per (raceId, driverId) or when they have been aggregated to that grain. If qualifying is one-to-many (multiple attempts), pre-aggregate qualifying attempts (e.g., best_time per raceId/driverId) before joining to avoid duplicating result-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to qualifying_with_driver_constructor or other one-row-per-(raceId,driverId) siblings on (raceId, driverId) — safe when target sibling is at same grain. | do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many detail without re-aggregation: examples include raw lap_times or any table with multiple rows per (raceId, driverId) (if present). Such joins will multiply rows and therefore over-count measures like points, laps, milliseconds unless you either (a) aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per (raceId, driverId) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate and compute measures with appropriate DISTINCT/averaging logic. | do NOT join to a constructors table that is one-to-many per constructorId (e.g., if a constructor dimension were duplicated) — only join to a constructors dimension that is one-row-per constructorId. If the constructor side is one-to-many, collapse it first to one row per constructorId. | When composing aggregates from this view: treat points, laps, milliseconds as additive measures over the view's grain (raceId, driverId). For driver-level totals, group by driverId and sum(points); for race-level summaries, group by raceId and sum(points) or compute aggregates across result rows.

params.description: Row-level race result facts for each driver result (one row per resultId) including finishing position, points, lap/time stats, and status.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve detailed result facts for a single result, driver, race, or constructor (filter by resultId, driverId, raceId, constructorId). | Compose aggregated race-level or driver-level metrics by grouping this view (e.g., total points per driver, number of podiums per driver). | Join to driver, race, constructor, or circuit dimension views to enrich result facts with descriptive attributes. | Filter or analyze fastest-lap and timing metrics at the result-row granularity (e.g., compare fastestLapTime across results).
params.output_schema: resultId: unique identifier of the result row (derived from results.resultId) | raceId: foreign key to the race in which this result occurred (derived from results.raceId) | driverId: foreign key to the driver who achieved this result (derived from results.driverId) | constructorId: foreign key to the constructor for this result (derived from results.constructorId) | points: championship points awarded for this result (derived from results.points) | position: finishing position as stored in results.position (derived from results.position) | positionText: textual finishing position as stored in results.positionText (derived from results.positionText) | positionOrder: numeric ordering of finishing position used for ordering results (derived from results.positionOrder) | laps: number of laps completed in this result (derived from results.laps) | time: textual total race time as stored in results.time (derived from results.time) | milliseconds: total race time in milliseconds (derived from results.milliseconds) | fastestLap: fastest lap number for this result (derived from results.fastestLap) | rank: rank of this result's fastest lap within the session (derived from results.rank) | fastestLapTime: fastest lap time for this result as text (derived from results.fastestLapTime) | fastestLapSpeed: speed recorded for the fastest lap (derived from results.fastestLapSpeed) | statusId: foreign key to result status (derived from results.statusId)
params.grounded_columns: results.resultId | results.raceId | results.driverId | results.constructorId | results.points | results.position | results.positionText | results.positionOrder | results.laps | results.time | results.milliseconds | results.fastestLap | results.rank | results.fastestLapTime | results.fastestLapSpeed | results.statusId
params.metric: points = results.points (atomic numeric measure stored at the resultId grain) | laps = results.laps (atomic count of laps for the resultId) | milliseconds = results.milliseconds (atomic timing measure in ms at resultId) | fastestLap = results.fastestLap (atomic lap number for fastest lap at resultId) | fastestLapTime = results.fastestLapTime (atomic fastest-lap time string at resultId) | fastestLapSpeed = results.fastestLapSpeed (atomic speed measure for fastest lap at resultId)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to drivers_core (or drivers_base / drivers_core) on driverId — safe because driver dimensions are one-row-per-driver; joining enriches this view without duplicating result measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to races_core (or race_rows / race_with_circuit) on raceId — safe because races are one-row-per-race; result-level measures remain one-per-result. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (or circuits_core_7) through race_with_circuit (join driver_results.raceId -> race_with_circuit.raceId then race_with_circuit.circuitId -> circuits_core.circuitId) — safe if the race_with_circuit and circuits_core are one-row-per-race / one-row-per-circuit respectively. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to qualifying_with_driver_ref or qualifying_with_driver_constructor on (raceId, driverId) only if those sibling views are one-row-per-(raceId,driverId) attempt; if they are one-to-many (multiple qualifying attempts), results measures would be multiplied and you must aggregate qualifying rows first or de-duplicate before joining. | DO NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views such as qualifying_attempts (multiple attempts per (raceId,driverId)) directly to this view if you intend to preserve the result-level measures (points, milliseconds, laps). Joining directly will multiply result rows and thus multiply measures. Instead, aggregate qualifying_attempts to one row per (raceId,driverId) (e.g., min/fastest attempt) or compute derived metrics before joining. | When composing aggregations: to compute higher-level metrics (e.g., total points per driver or per constructor), GROUP BY driverId or constructorId on this view — do not join additional one-to-many detail before the aggregation unless you re-aggregate the joined detail to avoid duplication. | If you need to join another one-to-many detail and preserve correct metrics, use lateral/row_number/deduplication strategies or join pre-aggregated subqueries keyed at resultId or (raceId,driverId) so each resultId remains unique in the joined result set.

If you derive metrics on top of this view, define them explicitly, for example: qualifying_count = COUNT(qualifying_attempts.qualifyId) when joining qualifying_attempts grouped by raceId.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to circuits_core (or other circuit dimension views) on circuitId — safe because races_with_circuit_info is already one-row-per-race and the join to a one-row-per-circuit dimension (circuits_core) will not duplicate race rows. | Safe to join to race_rows or race_results on raceId when you intend to bring race-level attributes into those multi-row-per-race result sets; in that case the multi-row side determines multiplicity, not this view (this view will not multiply the result beyond the existing rows per race). | Do NOT join races_with_circuit_info directly to one-to-many fact tables (e.g., qualifying_attempts, race_results, pit_stops) expecting to preserve race-level aggregates — such joins will multiply rows per race and thus duplicate any race-level measures. Instead, either: | - aggregate the fact table first to race-level (GROUP BY raceId) and then join to this view on raceId; or | - perform the join and then re-aggregate, e.g., SELECT r.*, COUNT(f.*) AS metric FROM races_with_circuit_info r JOIN fact f USING(raceId) GROUP BY r.raceId, r.year, r.round, r.name, r.date, r.circuitId, r.circuit_name, r.circuit_location, r.circuit_country. | Do NOT join to other one-to-many views (e.g., qualifying_with_driver_ref, qualifying_with_driver_constructor) without re-aggregation or selecting the appropriate grain — those views are multi-row per race and would multiply race-level rows unless you aggregate them to raceId first. | When composing multiple joins, ensure exactly one side is at the one-row-per-race grain (this view or an aggregated result). If you need race-level attributes together with driver-level or attempt-level details, keep this view as the race dimension and perform joins from the many-side (drivers/results) to it, accepting the result will have many rows per race.
